items.title: Adani Group eyes airline investments months after ruling out airline entry
items.rss_summary: The diversified Adani group, which runs multiple airports across the country, has requested the government to allow it to invest in the airline sector, a top official said on Friday. Group chief finance officer Jugeshinder Robbie Singh told reporters that over 60 crore people in the country can fly, and the number of daily flights needs to go up by nearly 10 times to 30,000. "And that's why we requested the government to at least allow us to invest, so that we can facilitate the development of airlines. Some fund, some other airline company and things like that...or an entrepreneur who wants to go into that space," the CFO said while speaking on the sidelines of the India Debt Capital Market Summit here. In July this year, the group said it was "not evaluating any proposal to enter the airlines business". items.title: BPCL commissions integrated lube blending plant, base oil terminal in Maha
items.rss_summary: Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) has commissioned an integrated lube oil blending plant and base oil terminal at Rasayani in Maharashtra, strengthening its manufacturing and supply-chain infrastructure as the state-run energy major seeks to expand its MAK Lubricants business. The facilities, inaugurated on November 21 by BPCL chairman and managing director Sanjay Khanna, bring together base oil receipt and storage, lubricant blending, product filling, warehousing and dispatch within a single integrated operational complex, according to a company statement. The new infrastructure is expected to improve manufacturing flexibility, inventory management and supply reliability, while allowing BPCL to respond more efficiently to changing customer requirements and market demand.
